name: Modal (VM Sandboxes)

modes.label: VM Sandbox, request = size
modes.note: Priced on Modal's own published unit: "The `cpu` parameter specifies physical CPU cores (1 core = 2 vCPUs)" (modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources, checked 2026-11-08). $0.00003942 per core-second = $0.070956 per vCPU-hour; memory $0.00000667 per GiB-second (modal.com/pricing). A 4 vCPU / 8 GiB sandbox = cpu=2, memory 8192 = $0.283824 + $0.192096 = $0.47592/h. Rates include the 3x non-preemptible multiplier over Function rates. Billed per second on max(request, actual): "You're charged `max(request, actual)` for both CPU and memory." Sandboxes burst above the request when the host has spare capacity; set a cpu limit to cap the burst, or bursting can bill above 2 cores. Caveat, not the price: StarSling measured cpu=N with a matching limit gives nproc N in the guest (hpc-sandbox-benchmarks PR #121, https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/pull/121). Speed rows measured at cpu=4 are therefore not like for like with this 2-core price. VM runtime (runtime="vm"): same per-second CPU and memory rates as the gVisor sandboxes (https://modal.com/blog/vm-sandboxes-agent-computers).
modes.perf_source: VM runtime (runtime="vm"). StarSling requested cpu=4 and the sandbox saw 4 CPUs (https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/pull/121); Modal prices 1 physical core = 2 vCPU, so match price and speed with care. ComputeSDK has no VM-runtime row. CPU 15.48 runs/s: V8 Web Tooling Benchmark (Phoronix node-web-tooling), StarSling hpc-sandbox-benchmarks run 37073680030 (2026-10-03), row "Modal (VM)", median of 5 sandboxes at a 4 vCPU / 8 GB target, rank 7 of 15 (shared: the run cannot separate it from the providers at the same rank). https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/blob/297198a96ee827df5edcd918bd37b949526cfe20/LEADERBOARD.md

modes.label: VM Sandbox, minimal request + burst
modes.note: The request is set to the minimum (cpu 0.125 core = 0.25 vCPU; 128 MiB) and cpu/memory limits are set to the workload size. Billing is max(request, actual) per second, so it tracks usage. active_floor 0.0625 = 0.25 vCPU / 4 vCPU (the exact floor is 0.25/W.vcpu). Burst capacity is not guaranteed (it needs spare host capacity), so the workload can be throttled. The memory limit is a hard OOM, and Modal can evict a sandbox that uses more memory than it requested (docs recommend requesting p90-95 of memory), so the RAM half of this regime is optimistic. Floor: 'minimum of 0.125 cores per container' (modal.com/pricing); 'a default request of 0.125 CPU cores and 128 MiB of memory' (modal.com/docs/guide/resources). Price unit: 1 core = 2 vCPUs (modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources, checked 2026-11-08). Caveat, not the price: StarSling measured cpu=N with a matching limit gives nproc N in the guest (hpc-sandbox-benchmarks PR #121, https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/pull/121). Speed rows measured at cpu=4 are therefore not like for like with this 2-core price. VM runtime (runtime="vm"): same per-second CPU and memory rates as the gVisor sandboxes (https://modal.com/blog/vm-sandboxes-agent-computers).
modes.perf_source: VM runtime (runtime="vm"). StarSling requested cpu=4 and the sandbox saw 4 CPUs (https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/pull/121); Modal prices 1 physical core = 2 vCPU, so match price and speed with care. ComputeSDK has no VM-runtime row. CPU 15.48 runs/s: V8 Web Tooling Benchmark (Phoronix node-web-tooling), StarSling hpc-sandbox-benchmarks run 37073680030 (2026-10-03), row "Modal (VM)", median of 5 sandboxes at a 4 vCPU / 8 GB target, rank 7 of 15 (shared: the run cannot separate it from the providers at the same rank). https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/blob/297198a96ee827df5edcd918bd37b949526cfe20/LEADERBOARD.md

evidence.quote: By default, Sandboxes can make outbound connections to any public IP address.
prevent the Sandbox from making any outbound connections

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: $30/mo included compute; max 3 seats (no paid extra seats listed); 100 containers, 10 GPU concurrency; egress 1 TiB/mo free; payment method required; overage auto-charged (spend limit optional, hard stop). GPU concurrency 10 (modal.com/pricing, 2026-09-28); non-spec key gpu_concurrency (engine plan.concurrency holds the 100-container cap).

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $250/month fee with $100/month of free credits; unlimited seats; 5,000 containers, 50 GPU concurrency; egress 10 TiB/mo free (engine network block uses Starter's 1 TiB); static IP proxy; custom domains; environment budgets.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom pricing: volume discounts, compute reservations, AWS/GCP marketplace committed spend; egress 100 TiB/mo free; HIPAA compatibility (Enterprise only; no BAA named on the pricing page), SSO, audit logs; 100k+ concurrent sandboxes cited in Modal blog.

perf_source: Two runtimes (VM here, gVisor on the card "Modal"): perf is per mode.

knobs.label: Region pin

options.label: Broad region pin: us / eu / ap (×1.15)
Narrow region pin: us-east, uk, jp ... (×1.75)

knobs.why: Modal multiplies all sandbox resource charges by 1.15x for a broad-region pin and 1.75x for a narrow-region pin; data residency (e.g. EU) requires a pin.

knobs.label: Idle time billed before idle_timeout / timeout ends the sandbox (× session hours)
knobs.why: Modal has no paused state: an idle sandbox pays its full request (max(request, actual)) until idle_timeout or timeout (default 5 min, max 24 h) terminates it, or you call terminate(). Default 1 = you terminate as soon as work ends; the 2x ceiling is a judgment call.

caveats: How we count Modal's CPU: same rule as the "Modal" card. We use Modal's own unit, 1 physical core = 2 vCPU, the lowest Modal price its own pages support: 4 vCPU / 8 GiB = cpu=2 = $0.47592/h. cpu=N gives the sandbox N CPUs, so if your code needs 4 CPUs, request cpu=4: $0.759744/h at 8 GiB. Rule: FAIRNESS.md, 'CPU units'.

Generally available since 2026-10-01, announced at Modal's Runtime conference: "Today we’re making VM Sandboxes generally available on Modal, built for those who need to give their agents the power of a full computer." (https://modal.com/blog/vm-sandboxes-agent-computers). Early customers (Linear Coding Sessions, Legora evals, Snorkel simulations) launched over 20 million VMs before GA.

Same API and prices as the gVisor sandboxes (card "Modal"); split out because the runtimes differ: a VM with its own Linux kernel on Cloud Hypervisor here (Docker, FUSE, eBPF, systemd, nested cgroups), GPUs only on gVisor.
No GPUs on this runtime: "GPU Sandboxes are only supported with runtime=\"gvisor\"". Use the gVisor runtime of the same provider for GPUs.

Set runtime="vm" explicitly to get this card's runtime: "Switch runtimes via the `runtime` parameter, or leave unset to let Modal choose for you." (https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandboxes#runtimes, checked 2026-10-14).
Nested virtualization: Enterprise plan only, as an experimental option (experimental_options={"enable_nested_virt": True}) (https://modal.com/docs/guide/vm-sandboxes, checked 2026-11-08).

Memory snapshots are alpha: snapshotting terminates the sandbox, they expire after 7 days, no GPUs, restore needs the same instance type, and the region cannot be pinned. Modal recommends them with runtime="vm" (https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-snapshots, checked 2026-11-08).

Files after the sandbox ends: call snapshot_filesystem() and boot the next sandbox from that image (root filesystem incl. /var/lib/docker; 30-day default TTL, or ttl=None for indefinite), or mount a Volume. Volumes are not part of a filesystem snapshot.
Root filesystem on VMs is a fixed 512 GiB and cannot be increased (https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources, checked 2026-11-08).
Sidecars (beta) work on VMs but not with memory bursting: sidecar memory is reserved up front.
Sandboxes run 24 h at most; Modal recommends filesystem snapshots to continue longer work in a new sandbox.
free.monthly_credit ($30) IS the Starter plan's included_usd, so don't subtract both. Team replaces it with $100 included.
Burst above the request bills above the requested size when no cpu limit is set (default soft limit is request + 16 cores). The engine cannot model this; set cpu=(req, limit).

Egress is $0.04/GiB beyond the plan allowance (Starter 1 TiB, Team 10 TiB, Enterprise 100 TiB per month). The allowance counts private container-to-container traffic and Cloud Bucket Mount uploads. The engine network block uses the Starter allowance. https://modal.com/docs/guide/network-egress-billing
GPU sandboxes are preemptible. GPU concurrency is 10 (Starter) and 50 (Team). H100->H200 and A100-40->80 auto-upgrades are billed at the requested type's price.
Enterprise discounts and reservations are unpublished. Startup credits are unpublished. Academic grants are up to $10k one-time (not in free.one_time_credit).

GPU concurrency caps: Starter 10, Team 50, Enterprise custom (modal.com/pricing, 2026-09-28). The engine plan concurrency is the container cap (100 / 5,000); a workload with >10 concurrent GPU sandboxes needs Team.

Included compute ($30 Starter / $100 Team) applies to Functions, Sandboxes and Notebooks CPU/memory/GPU; Volumes have their own 1 TiB; Shared Endpoint tokens are billed from the first request (since 2026-09-01). Whether egress overage is covered by included compute is not stated.

fleet.tiers: Starter 100 concurrent containers / 10 GPUs; Team ($250/month) 5,000 containers / 50 GPUs; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: Pricing checked against current official page; old 1,000 Team-container claims are stale. 10/50 CPU fleet fits Starter, 300/1,000 Team within quota, not a reservation. GPU count is total GPUs concurrently used, confirmed by scale guide, not GPU-container count. Per-Function hard cap 4,000 distinct from workspace total. No approval SLA. New-account spend ceiling: the Workspace budget maximum grows only after successful incremental charges, and usage stops at the limit. SDK 1.6.0 (2026-09-28) made the v2 Sandbox backend default with 'substantially higher creation rates and concurrency limits for CPU Sandboxes'; Sandbox.create raises ResourceExhaustedError if unschedulable. No numeric creation-rate limit is published; the pricing page still lists 100 (Starter) / 5000 (Team) containers.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshots are triggered from outside the Sandbox, typically just before termination.
snapshot_auto.note: Timeout (max 24 h) and idle_timeout terminate the sandbox; no pause/sleep state and no automatic checkpoint. Docs tell you to call snapshot_filesystem() yourself before terminating and restore into a new sandbox.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Sandbox memory snapshots are copies of a Sandbox’s entire state, both in memory and on the filesystem. These Snapshots can be restored later to create a new Sandbox, which is an exact clone of the original Sandbox.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Filesystem snapshots (snapshot_filesystem(), disk only, become Images that boot any number of new sandboxes; 30-day default TTL, ttl=None for indefinite) and directory snapshots (snapshot_directory). Memory snapshots (alpha): RAM + FS, snapshotting terminates the sandbox, no GPU, 7-day expiry, same instance type, no region pin.

harness_api.quote: Run a background coding agent with OpenCode
harness_api.note: Only examples (OpenCode server, Claude Agent SDK, Cursor Cloud Agents) built on generic exec/tunnels; no first-party API to start/stream/resume a harness. Modal is an execution backend for Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents (harness driven by Anthropic, not a Modal API). Sidecars doc mentions 'Separating an agent harness from its execution environment' as a pattern only.

egress_allowlist.quote:
| **IP-range allowlist**        | `outbound_cidr_allowlist`   | Only allows traffic to the listed CIDR ranges (any protocol).  |
| **Domain allowlist** *(Beta)* | `outbound_domain_allowlist` | Only allows TLS traffic (port 443) to the listed domain names. |
egress_allowlist.note: Also block_network=True (no internet). Domain allowlist is SNI-based (beta, wildcards), Modal resolves hostname itself; experimental runtime updates of allowlists without restart.

egress_http_rules.quote: TLS traffic is not decrypted, so the `Host` header, URL path, and body are never inspected.
egress_http_rules.note: Built-in controls are host/IP only. DIY option: experimental proxy_traffic_via_sidecar routes all port-443 traffic to a user-run Sidecar (alpha, allowlisted workspaces) where you can run e.g. mitmproxy for method/path filtering; that is user-operated, not a provider rule engine.

ingress_rules.quote:
Use `inbound_cidr_allowlist` to restrict which IP addresses can connect
**inbound** to the Sandbox through tunnels and Sandbox Connect Tokens:
ingress_rules.note: Default: no inbound. Ports exposed explicitly (encrypted_ports/h2_ports/unencrypted_ports); Sandbox Connect Tokens give authenticated HTTP/WebSocket access with an unspoofable X-Verified-User-Data header.

guest_firewall.quote: **VMs** run the Sandbox in a virtual machine with its own Linux kernel.
guest_firewall.note: Derived for the VM runtime (runtime="vm", GA since 2026-10-01) with root. The gVisor runtime (root, own netstack) does not document iptables support.

secret_proxy.quote: The Sandbox is told where the proxy is but is given no Secrets.
secret_proxy.how: run your own credential-injecting proxy in a Sidecar that holds the Secret (official example; Sidecars are experimental)

volume_attach.quote: Volumes are a high-performance distributed file system for Modal applications.
volume_attach.note: modal.Volume mounted via volumes={...} on Sandbox.create; also CloudBucketMount (S3/R2/GCS). VM sandboxes: "named Images and Volumes can be used just as with Functions" (modal.com/docs/guide/vm-sandboxes). Volumes are not included in filesystem snapshots.

volume_shared.quote:
Concurrent modification from multiple containers is supported, but concurrent
modifications of the same files should be avoided. Last write wins
volume_shared.note: Read-write (or read_only mount option); sub_path mounts isolate sessions on one Volume; v2 volumes: concurrent writes from hundreds of containers. Changes visible to others only after commit + reload. Bucket mounts also shareable.

docker_inside.quote: Use the VM runtime to run Docker in a Sandbox.

anti_bot.quote: Modal is a platform for running AI workloads in the cloud with minimal configuration. Key use cases include AI model training and inference, high-performance batch jobs, and sandboxed code execution.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Modal is a general compute/sandbox platform, not a browser-automation/scraping product; no stealth or fingerprint-evasion feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Modal is a platform for running AI workloads in the cloud with minimal configuration. Key use cases include AI model training and inference, high-performance batch jobs, and sandboxed code execution.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature or API is documented anywhere in Modal's docs/pricing.

egress_ip_type.quote: Proxies are a secure tunnel between Apps and exit nodes with static IPs. You can allow-list those static IPs in your network firewall...
egress_ip_type.note: Team/Enterprise-plan Proxy feature gives fixed outbound datacenter IPs (WireGuard exit nodes); default (no Proxy) egress uses Modal's shared cloud-provider datacenter IP ranges, which vary by run.

fork_running.quote: Since Filesystem Snapshots are Images, you can create multiple Sandboxes from the same snapshot.
fork_running.note: The page does not say whether the source sandbox keeps running after snapshot_filesystem(): every example calls terminate() right after it. Memory snapshots copy RAM but "Snapshotting a Sandbox will currently cause it to terminate." Not confirmed either way; same value as the gVisor card.

wake_on_request.quote: Sandboxes can also be automatically terminated after a period of inactivity - you can do this by setting the `idle_timeout` parameter.
wake_on_request.note: Sandboxes have no sleep/paused state: idle_timeout or timeout fully terminates the Sandbox (Finished state); there is no mechanism for a stopped sandbox to wake automatically on an incoming request. Consistent with card caveat 'No pause/stopped state.'

live_resize.quote: Physical core (2 vCPU equivalent)... You pay for max(request, actual). ... a default request of 0.125 CPU cores and 128 MiB of memory
live_resize.note: CPU/memory are set via request/limit parameters at Sandbox.create() time (with elastic bursting up to a limit); no documented API to change a running Sandbox's resource request/limit after creation without recreating it. The Sandbox SDK reference (Sandbox.md) has no update/resize method.

own_agent_api.quote: Modal is a platform for running AI workloads in the cloud with minimal configuration. Key use cases include AI model training and inference, high-performance batch jobs, and sandboxed code execution.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Modal is an execution backend that lets customers run their own agents/harnesses (examples: OpenCode, Claude Agent SDK, Cursor Cloud Agents); it does not ship its own first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: This example demonstrates how to deploy a simple MCP server on Modal with FastMCP.
mcp_server.note: Modal's MCP-related material is an example of hosting a user-built MCP server on Modal, not a first-party MCP server Modal ships to let clients control Modal Sandboxes/Apps themselves. No such control-plane MCP server is documented in the CLI or guide sections of llms.txt.

lang_node.quote: Modal offers official SDKs in Python, Go, and JavaScript/TypeScript, along with a fully-featured CLI for interacting with the platform.
lang_node.note: First-party JS/TypeScript SDK (modal.com/docs/sdk/js/latest/intro.md, beta) exposes Sandbox/Function/etc.; Node.js also runs inside sandboxes generically via custom images (e.g. 'Run Node.js, Ruby, and more in a Sandbox' example).

byoc.quote: Compute jobs at Modal are containerized and virtualized using gVisor... Sandboxes may also run on Modal's secure VM runtime.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Modal is a fully managed multi-tenant serverless platform running on its own infrastructure/regions; no self-hosted-in-your-cloud-account (BYOC) deployment option is documented on the security, pricing, or enterprise pages.

eu_data_residency.quote: You can select the container and routing regions for most Modal services... For a full list of available regions, please visit our region selection documentation page.
eu_data_residency.note: Region selection documents an 'eu' broad region (European Economic Area) with eu-west/eu-north/eu-south narrow regions; Sandboxes support container-region pinning to 'eu' (region-selection.md), which the card's region-broad/region-narrow modes price at 1.15x/1.75x.

persistent_disk.quote: Filesystem Snapshots are copies of the Sandbox's root filesystem at a given point in time.
persistent_disk.how: snapshot the root filesystem before the sandbox ends and boot the next sandbox from it; Volumes also keep files across sandboxes

pause_resume.quote: If you need a Sandbox to run for more than 24 hours, we recommend using Filesystem Snapshots to preserve its state, and then restore from that snapshot with a subsequent Sandbox.
pause_resume.note: No pause API on VMs: keep state with a filesystem snapshot and start a new sandbox from it (new sandbox, disk only).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The new Sandbox will be a duplicate of your original Sandbox. All running processes will still be running, in the same state as when they were snapshotted, and any changes made to the filesystem will be visible.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Memory Snapshots (alpha, experimental API _experimental_snapshot / _experimental_enable_snapshot) capture RAM+FS and Sandbox._experimental_from_snapshot() clones them into a new, running Sandbox with processes' memory state intact. No longer documented as on-request for VMs (checked 2026-10-14). Snapshotting terminates the source sandbox, so this is a clone-on-restore, not a fork of a still-running original.

nested_virt.quote: Nested virtualization is available on the Enterprise plan ... by setting `experimental_options={"enable_nested_virt": True}` on a VM Sandbox.
nested_virt.note: Enterprise plan only, as an experimental option.

ssh.quote: This can be used to SSH into a container (see example below).
ssh.how: install openssh-server in the image, run sshd and expose port 22 as an unencrypted tunnel (official example)
ssh.note: Documented pattern, not a managed SSH endpoint: you supply sshd and keys. The example lines: .apt_install("openssh-server"), subprocess.Popen(["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D", "-e"]). Same value as the gVisor card.

desktop.quote: In each Sandbox, Xvfb provides a virtual display, x11vnc serves it over VNC, and websockify bridges the stream into the noVNC page that the UI embeds.
desktop.how: install Xvfb, x11vnc and noVNC in the sandbox image (official runnable example)

browser.quote: The agent drives Chromium inside a Modal Sandbox running in a VM.
browser.how: install Chromium in the sandbox image (official runnable example)

computer_use.quote: Computer-use agents are LLMs that can interact with a web browser in a loop. ... This example builds one with Browser Use.
computer_use.how: run a computer-use agent (Browser Use) on the VNC desktop from the official example

public_ipv4.quote: Sandboxes are built to be secure-by-default, meaning that a default Sandbox has no ability to accept incoming network connections or access your Modal resources.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is only via TLS tunnels/hostnames (modal.forward, encrypted_ports, Connect Tokens) or workspace-private i6pn IPv6 for clusters; there is no per-sandbox public IPv4 assigned. The 'static IP' feature (Proxies, already features.static_egress_ip=true) is for outbound traffic only ('Proxies are a secure tunnel between Apps and exit nodes with static IPs'), not an inbound public IPv4 on the machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: The bot runs on Modal and uses the Claude Agent SDK ... it runs inside a Modal Sandbox
agent_harnesses.how: install the agent harness in the sandbox image yourself (official examples: Claude Agent SDK, Cursor Cloud Agents)

windows.quote: By default, Modal Functions and Sandboxes run in a Debian Linux environment with a basic Python installation of the same minor version `v3.x` as your local Python interpreter.
windows.note: No Windows runtime or Windows base images are offered anywhere in the docs; Sandboxes/Functions are Linux containers/VMs (Debian-based, or custom OCI Linux images) only.

macos.quote: By default, Modal Functions and Sandboxes run in a Debian Linux environment
macos.note: Modal is a Linux-container/VM compute platform (gVisor or Linux-kernel VM runtimes); no macOS machines/images are offered. Plainly outside the product, matching the 'macOS for a GPU cloud' example in the field definitions.

arm64.quote: The image must be built for the `linux/amd64` platform.
arm64.note: Docs require linux/amd64 for custom images and never mention arm64/aarch64/Graviton/Apple-silicon guest CPUs anywhere in the docs, GPU guide, or pricing page; the only architecture named across the full llms-full.txt corpus is x86_64/amd64 (e.g. flash-attn wheels are linux_x86_64, binaries are linux-amd64). Treated as x86_64-only.

self_host.quote: Most interactions with Modal are well-described in a gRPC API, and occur through modal, our open-source command-line tool and Python client library.
self_host.note: Only the client (CLI/SDK) is open; the actual compute platform (workers, scheduler, storage) is Modal's own multi-tenant SaaS with no on-prem/self-hosted or BYOC deployment option documented anywhere (Enterprise plan mentions AWS/GCP marketplace billing, not deploying Modal's control plane into a customer's account).

open_source.quote: occur through modal, our open-source command-line tool and Python client library.
open_source.note: Only the `modal` CLI/Python client is open-source; the core product -- the compute platform itself (scheduler, workers, storage, billing) -- is closed-source and only usable as Modal's hosted service. No OSI license covers the core product.

cpu_class.quote: Sandboxes can burst beyond their CPU and memory requests when additional resources are available on the underlying host. Your request guarantees a minimum level of resources, but when spare capacity exists, your Sandbox can use more. You pay for `max(request, actual)`.
cpu_class.note: Modal guarantees the requested number of physical cores ('access to at least N cores', modal.com/docs/guide/resources) -- i.e. reserved/dedicated capacity up to the request, with additional cores above that available only opportunistically (soft limit request+16 cores, throttled beyond it) and billed via max(request,actual). For on-demand/region-*/vm-sandbox modes the request is set to the workload size, so the guaranteed (dedicated) portion covers the whole workload. For low-request-burst the request is deliberately set to the minimum (0.125 core) and the card's own note says burst capacity is NOT guaranteed ('it needs spare host capacity ... the workload may be throttled'), so most of that mode's effective vCPUs are best-effort/shared rather than reserved.

fast_boot.quote: This brings the same APIs, `modal.Image`s, sub-second cold-starts, and CPU/memory bursting capabilities as previously
fast_boot.note: fast_boot means benchmarked. The old evidence was the ComputeSDK burst row, which runs Modal's default (gVisor) runtime; ComputeSDK burst_tti 2026-11-06 has no VM-runtime row. Modal claims sub-second cold starts for VMs, but no published 100-at-once measurement exists. gVisor: card "Modal" (benchmarked, true).

usage_api.quote: The card lists billing and budgets guides as sources but does not provide specific evidence of a REST API, SDK method, or CLI command that returns per-sandbox or per-tag billable usage. Modal's pricing page and billing docs do not document a programmatic usage/metrics endpoint in the available card
usage_api.note: Modal ships a Python SDK and CLI but the card's sources do not cite a specific usage_api endpoint, method, or CLI command. Verification requires checking modal.com/docs/guide/billing and the SDK reference directly for methods like get_usage(), usage API endpoints, or billing export formats. The card's 'budgets' feature (plan-level spend limits) is documented but distinct from usage reporting.

persist_scope.quote: Filesystem Snapshots are copies of the Sandbox's root filesystem at a given point in time. ... Filesystem Snapshots now default to a 30-day TTL. You can configure a custom TTL when creating a snapshot, or opt out of expiry entirely to retain snapshots indefinitely.
persist_scope.how: call snapshot_filesystem() before the sandbox ends, then start the next sandbox from that image (ttl=None keeps it indefinitely); or mount a Volume for files that must survive

isolation.quote: Starting from the Rust-based Cloud Hypervisor project, we layered on a half dozen innovations spanning our host filesystems, lazy image loading, memory bursting, and snapshotting tech.

fuse.quote: Use the VM runtime for workloads that expect a full Linux environment, such as running Docker inside the Sandbox, mounting FUSE filesystems, or managing resources with nested cgroups.

kernel_features.quote: They run a real Linux kernel, so they can support workloads that run Docker containers within the Sandbox, or that require Linux features like eBPF, systemd, cgroups, or custom filesystem mounts.

gpu.quote: GPU Sandboxes are only supported with `runtime="gvisor"`.
gpu.note: GPUs are offered on the gVisor runtime of the same provider (card "Modal").

snapshot.quote: Memory snapshots are supported on both runtimes, and we recommend using memory snapshots with `runtime="vm"`.
snapshot.note: Memory snapshots (RAM + FS) are alpha: snapshotting terminates the sandbox, they expire after 7 days, no GPUs, restore needs the same instance type, and the region cannot be pinned. The page states no Volume rule for VMs. Filesystem snapshots (30-day default TTL, or indefinite) and directory snapshots work for everyone.

sidecar.quote: Sandbox Sidecars let you run additional containers alongside your main Sandbox container, on the same host.
sidecar.note: Beta. Works on VMs, but "cannot be combined with memory bursting": reserve sidecar memory up front (vm_sidecar_memory_reserve_mib).

hipaa.note: Enterprise plan only: the pricing table ticks HIPAA compatibility for Enterprise, not Starter or Team. The pricing page does not mention a BAA.

burst.quote: Sandboxes can burst beyond their CPU and memory requests when additional resources are available on the underlying host. Your request guarantees a minimum level of resources, but when spare capacity exists, your Sandbox can use more. You pay for `max(request, actual)`.
burst.note: Billed per second for max(request, used): a sandbox can use more than it reserved. Bursting is best effort, not guaranteed capacity.

snapshot_mem.quote: Memory snapshots are supported on both runtimes, and we recommend using memory snapshots with `runtime="vm"`.
snapshot_mem.note: Alpha, experimental API (_experimental_enable_snapshot / _experimental_snapshot). Limits: terminates the source sandbox, 7-day expiry, no GPUs, same instance type on restore, no region pin.

whole_disk.quote: Note that a Filesystem Snapshot only covers the Sandbox's root filesystem.
